questions.text: What would happen if your own needs mattered just as much as the comfort of the people around you?
How do you gently return to yourself when you notice you are standing in familiar footsteps that do not belong to your future?
Where does your body store the quiet weight of all the things you swallowed instead of saying?
What allows you to hold onto the truth of your experience even while offering an apology to someone else?
What part of you is waiting to be forgiven for simply having a breaking point?
Who in your world sees the person beneath the caregiver?
What does your mind whisper to you when you finally give yourself permission to stop?
